answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may place orders, with one bond backing only one active identity at a time. When counterparties report a provable breach—such as failing to deliver after escrow—the protocol burns part of that bond and rewards the reporter. This does not make sybils impossible, but makes them costly: an attacker must tie up capital for every identity and risks losing it. Reputation can then grow only through completed trades, like an ember kept alight beneath a lantern on a trellis of verified exchanges.
